assessment: All four final visual comments are load-bearing and non-duplicative. They respectively establish continuous periodic DTFT geometry, the convolution/product duality, independent response of three eternal complex modes, and the local nonzero-band meaning of group delay. All are course-owned mathematical explanations rather than authenticity-bearing artifacts, so no sourced image is warranted.
scope_guardrail: Use engineering j, DTFT analysis exp(-j omega n), synthesis exp(+j omega n) with 1/(2 pi), radians/sample, and unit-circle notation X(e^(j omega)) and H(e^(j omega)). A continuous DTFT curve is asserted only for the finite record or an absolutely summable sequence. The mode-response sequence uses the FIR eigenfunction calculation directly for eternal modes and must not depict their spectra as ordinary continuous DTFTs. Phase and group delay are undefined at response zeros; phase is unwrapped only within a connected nonzero band. Transform multiplication is linear convolution under the stated existence conditions, never unpadded circular convolution or an FFT claim.

resolved_evidence_constraints: The frequency-circle visual is grounded only in x[n]=[1,2,-1], a finite and therefore absolutely summable sequence; its continuity caption must not generalize to every sequence.
The frequency seam is one point: omega=-pi and omega=+pi are the same endpoint, not two independent samples.
The convolution bridge states x,h in l1 and y=x*h, preserves the course sign and inverse scale, and explicitly excludes circular convolution.
The three-tap response values are exact: H(e^(j0))=1, H(e^(j pi/3))=(2/3)e^(-j pi/3), and H(e^(j 2pi/3))=0.
At the 2pi/3 null the mode output magnitude is zero while phase shift, phase delay, and group delay are undefined; no zero-phase label is allowed.
The eigenfunction statement applies to eternal complex modes. A causal gate would introduce partial-overlap transients and is outside the sequence visual.

Group delay is -d theta_H/d omega on a continuously unwrapped, differentiable phase branch where H is nonzero. The envelope interpretation also requires a sufficiently narrow occupied band and nearly constant magnitude across that band.

The packet comparison is a constructed local-response example, not measured data and not the three-tap averager; the displayed 5- and 20-sample delays must not be attributed to the averager, whose valid group delay is one sample away from its nulls.
house_style_adjustments: The convolution comment requests violet for y/Y, but the house palette permits currentColor plus amber, blue, and green. Use green for y/Y and name the role in text.

The configured course key image requires figures/dtft-frequency-circle.svg. Keep that first visual a simple raw SVG and replace its name-based embed with a src-based embed; reserve typeset multi-line formulas for the component bridge.
The two source inspirations are conceptual only. Recreate the convolution duality and packet-delay comparison in house style without tracing Osgood or MIT artwork.

constructed_data.time_alignment: Both input envelopes have reference center n=0; output reference centers are n=5 and n=20, with dashed input-envelope outlines retained for comparison.
constructed_data.packet_condition: Each occupied band is sufficiently narrow, H is nonzero and differentiable there, magnitude is approximately flat across it, and higher-order phase variation is negligible.
constructed_data.boundary: A separate response zero omega_z lies outside both occupied bands; theta_H(omega_z) and tau_g(omega_z) are undefined, and no unwrap line crosses the zero.
constructed_data.relationship_to_averager: This is a constructed comparison, not the three-tap averager. The averager has tau_g=1 sample on each connected nonzero interval and undefined group delay at +/-2pi/3.

figures.composition: Use a responsive two-tier comparison. The top tier shows a compact frequency strip with narrow occupied bands B1 and B2, both labelled local |H|=1, and two separate unwrapped phase tangent cards whose slopes are -5 and -20. A crossed null omega_z sits outside the brackets and is labelled phase/group delay undefined; no line bridges it. The bottom tier shows the two input packets aligned at n=0, then the blue output envelope centered at n=5 and amber output envelope centered at n=20, each with carrier oscillations and a dashed outline at the original center. On mobile, the frequency strip stays above two vertically stacked packet rows.

global_visual_rules.reading_order: left-to-right within mappings and packet time axes; top-to-bottom when component layouts stack on mobile
global_visual_rules.palette: currentColor plus amber #e2903a, blue #4c8dd6, and green #5aa46a only; the inline request for violet is normalized to green
global_visual_rules.theme_contract: Raw SVG text and support strokes use currentColor with opacity for secondary roles. Components use palette.ts and theme ink/muted values. No baked white background or fixed black text.
global_visual_rules.accessibility: Color is redundant with direct formula labels, row positions, phasor lengths/angles, crossed-null shape, B1/B2 headings, and numeric delay arrows. Alt text is one factual sentence and captions state one takeaway.
global_visual_rules.math_notation: Use j, n as integer sample index, m only as the convolution dummy, omega in radians/sample, X(e^(j omega)) and H(e^(j omega)) with parentheses, and tau_g(omega)=-d theta_H/d omega in samples. Do not abbreviate to H(omega) inside defining labels.
global_visual_rules.continuous_discrete_rule: Continuous frequency plots may use connected curves. Time-domain discrete sequences use stems/dots. The eigenmode sequence is a mode ledger, not an ordinary DTFT plot of an eternal sinusoid.
global_visual_rules.phase_boundary_rule: Display principal phase in (-pi,pi] only where a nonzero value needs it; use continuous unwrapped phase only within a connected nonzero region. At a zero print 'undefined' and break the branch.
global_visual_rules.convergence_rule: Qualify continuity with finite/l1 support, qualify the convolution theorem with x,h in l1, and qualify H eigenvalues with the FIR/stable-l1 impulse response. No visual may imply every formal Fourier series is an ordinary continuous function.
global_visual_rules.sourcing: All four figures visualize course-owned calculations or constructed comparisons. Osgood and MIT are inspiration for ideas only; none is an authenticity-bearing photograph, scan, or measured plot, so sourced_count is zero and no credits.yaml entry is needed.

phase zero, a phase arrow, or group delay reported at H=0
a sequence frame changing more than one newly active component
